contributions.headingText: Granular cell tumour is a neuroectodermal tumour composed of large, round to oval cells with abundant and distinctly eosinophilic granular cytoplasm.

9580/0 Granular cell tumour, NOS

9580/3 Granular cell tumour, malignant

2E89.1 & XH09A9 Benign tumours of uncertain differentiation, soft tissue & Granular cell tumour, NOS

2B5F.2 & XH90D3 Sarcoma, not elsewhere classified of other specified sites & Granular cell tumour, malignant
Not recommended: Abrikossoff tumour; granular cell myoblastoma; granular cell schwannoma.
Granular cell tumour occurs in any subcutaneous or submucosal site, but of the oral cases about 85% arise in the tongue {27918739; 31898368}.

Patients with granular cell tumour present with a non-tender, slowly enlarging, sessile mucosal to yellowish-coloured submucosal mass, usually < 10 mm in diameter (but they can be as large as 20 mm). Multifocal tumours occur infrequently {29661274; 32089415; 33253647}.
Granular cell tumours can present at any age, but most occur in the fourth to sixth decades of life, with an M:F ratio of 1:3 {31898368; 32189915}.

Sporadic oral granular cell tumours do not contain the PTPN11 and PTEN mutations {29097601} associated with granular cell tumours in LEOPARD syndrome (multiple lentigines, electrocardiographic conduction abnormalities, ocular hypertelorism, pulmonic stenosis, abnormal genitalia, retardation of growth, and sensorineural deafness), Noonan syndrome {19054014; 20537083; 22915371}, and PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome {12833416}. Whole-exome sequencing has revealed either mutations in the genes ATP6AP1, ATP6AP2, and ATP6V1A (components of the V-ATPase complex) {30166553; 33289181} or mutations in genes for endosomal/lysosomal/autophagosomal networks {33289181}. Overexpression of TFE3 is observed in skin lesions, but not in oral tumours {31788112}.
Granular cell tumour is a pale-tan to yellowish-white homogeneous submucosal nodule on cut surface {26637199; 32189915}.

Granular cell tumour is an unencapsulated tumour composed of large polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and small round nuclei in the subepithelial tissue. Granular cell tumours can grow in a syncytial pattern or be arranged in sheets surrounding and replacing muscle fascicles or nerves. Occasionally, granular cell tumours may be granular cell–poor with extensive fibrosis. Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia of the overlying mucosa is observed in 25–50% of cases {19192059; 33085297}, raising a risk of erroneous diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma in superficial biopsies. Criteria for malignancy in granular cell tumour include at least three of the following: nuclear pleomorphism, cell spindling, mitotic activity (> 2 mitoses/2 mm2), prominent nucleoli, a high N:C ratio, and necrosis. Cases meeting one or two of the criteria are classified as atypical {9669341}.

Immunohistochemistry

The tumour cells are immunoreactive for S100, CD57, SOX10, inhibin, and calretinin. CD68 highlights the cytoplasmic granules composed of lysosomes {26162589; 26637199; 29329562}. A rare non-neural granular cell tumour subtype is S100-negative and shows cell spindling, mitotic activity, rich vascularity, and an absence of pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia. Both subtypes are positive for NKI/C3 {27709427}.

Differential diagnosis

Granular cell tumour is relatively characteristic, but the differential diagnosis of other granular cell lesions is aided by immunohistochemistry {26637199; 32089415}.

Smears are usually cellular, with sheets of large cells with usually central, round to mildly pleomorphic nuclei and abundant granular cytoplasm, as well as a small number of single cells often resembling histiocytes, in a granular background {19526573}.

Essential: neoplastic sheets and nests of granular cells.

Desirable: pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia; S100 positivity.

Recurrence is rare after excision, even when the tumour is incompletely excised {31898368; 19192059; 33085297; 29661274}. Malignant granular cell tumour is associated with metastases and poor survival {24669168}.
